direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires pure Node ESM files in /output, manual argparse-compatible --a/--b parsing, no external modules, black-box behavior matching the executable, and hierarchical .mjs library structure.
Parallel metadata records actual parallel use with three subagents, artifact validation success, completed evaluation, and failed solution quality at 58 of 70 official cases.
Completed parallel status shows one AgentSwarm call, three subagent ids, expected output files, and official evaluator result solution_passed false with 58/70 cases.
Parallel evaluation summary confirms the official Docker evaluator completed successfully but the solution did not pass, with 58 passed samples out of 70.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream is transport/session metadata only for the parallel parent prompt, with no projected semantic events and a normal completed prompt.
Session index maps the parallel session id to the workspace session directory and confirms /workspace as the work directory.
Child agent-0 owned bech32core.mjs, wrote the library, hit an import failure after another child changed it, restored its verified version, retested, and warned the parent.
Child agent-1 owned segwit.mjs but found bech32core.mjs missing at its first check, wrote a fallback bech32core.mjs plus segwit.mjs, and passed local segwit tests.
Child agent-2 wrote cli.mjs and pyformat.mjs, tested parser and formatter behavior, cleaned its temporary test file, and reported only those modules as owned.

Parallel parent probed the executable, launched the three-child swarm, inspected child outputs and files, wrote test5.mjs, ran sample, fuzz, and CLI comparisons, cleaned temporary files, and finalized.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and requires pure ESM .mjs code, exact CLI behavior, black-box executable probing, and output files in /output.
Serial metadata records no parallel use, artifact validation success, completed evaluation, and failed solution quality at 58 of 70 official cases.
Completed serial status shows no delegation, expected output files, longer agent runtime than parallel, and official evaluator result solution_passed false with 58/70 cases.
Serial evaluation summary confirms the official Docker evaluator completed successfully but the solution did not pass, with 58 passed samples out of 70.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream is transport/session metadata only for the serial parent prompt, with no projected semantic events and a normal completed prompt.
Session index maps the serial session id to the workspace session directory and confirms /workspace as the work directory.

Serial main actor probed the executable, wrote all modules and entrypoint itself, tested sample and generated cases, found parser and length mismatches, patched them, reran comparisons, and finalized.

parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM .mjs output, local-only imports, manual --a/--b parsing, Python tuple formatting, bech32-only segwit decoding, uppercase acceptance, bech32m rejection, and executable-based verification.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent performed initial probes, delegated bech32 core, segwit decode, and CLI/format modules to three children, reserved entrypoint assembly and final verification for itself.
parallel.implementation: Children produced bech32core.mjs, segwit.mjs, cli.mjs, and pyformat.mjs; parent inspected those files, wrote test5.mjs, and kept the bech32 length check at <=90.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent read all four module files after the swarm, wrote the final entry file, cleaned scratch files, and delivered test5.mjs plus four library modules.
parallel.verification: Parallel run compared supplied examples, known valid/invalid vectors, 399 generated fuzz cases, and 13 CLI cases against the executable after child local tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 12 of 70 cases. The trajectory itself does not expose exact hidden failures; the parallel process also had a resolved child overwrite on bech32core.mjs.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, local-import, manual CLI, Python formatting, black-box matching, and hierarchical output requirements as the parallel run.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single main actor probed behavior, tracked todos, wrote all modules and the entrypoint, then iteratively patched the implementation based on comparisons.
serial.implementation: Serial produced a more granular module split and later removed the standard 90-character bech32 length restriction after discovering executable behavior on special long HRPs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial assembled the entrypoint and seven library modules in one workspace without subagents or cross-agent file ownership conflicts.
serial.verification: Serial compared samples, known vectors, 378 generated cases, 23 CLI cases, 36 special-HRP/long-address cases, 160 random-data cases, final samples, and syntax checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 12 of 70 cases even after local fixes. No raw trajectory evidence identifies the hidden failing cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the main migration obligations and also encoded the standard bech32 <=90 length rule in child work and final output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same obligations but later discovered the executable accepted some long addresses and removed the length cap.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both targeted the same task, but serial adjusted one black-box requirement from later probing while parallel retained the earlier standard-length assumption.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split ownership across three children: core bech32, segwit decode, and CLI/format, with parent owning final entrypoint and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all ownership in the main actor and used todos to sequence probing, implementation, entrypoint creation, and comparison.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split created overlapping ownership on bech32core.mjs through a fallback instruction; serial avoided that class of ownership conflict.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent specified exact exports for the core and segwit modules, but also let the segwit child create bech32core.mjs if missing, which undermined file ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial controlled all module interfaces locally and adjusted them directly after reading its own files during fixes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a cross-agent interface and ownership boundary around bech32core.mjs; serial had no child handoff or independent interface producer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delivered four modules and an entrypoint, with bech32core.mjs preserving a <=90 length restriction and segwit/CLI/format modules integrated by the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered seven smaller library modules and patched addressDecoder.mjs and constants.mjs to remove the length restriction after a failed special-HRP comparison.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial performed an additional implementation correction for long addresses; parallel did not, but both still failed the same official count.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent received the aggregate AgentSwarm result, inspected all child-written modules, then wrote the entrypoint and verified the integrated result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve and iterated directly through local reads, edits, tests, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No child result was abandoned in parallel; the notable lifecycle difference is the extra child-to-parent handoff and inspection step that serial did not need.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote to the same shared /output tree, and agent-1 overwrote agent-0's bech32core.mjs before agent-0 restored it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and edited its own files sequentially and used file reads before targeted edits; there was no cross-agent shared-state contention.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete source overwrite and recovery episode; serial's shared-state changes were ordinary sequential edits by one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran child local tests, then parent sample checks, generated fuzz comparisons, and CLI comparisons before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran repeated executable comparisons, found CLI and length mismatches, patched them, reran special and random matrices, and checked syntax.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's verification loop caught and fixed more ordinary behavioral mismatches; parallel's local and fuzz suite did not expose the official hidden failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in less agent time with three subagents and no timeout, but spent budget resolving the child source overwrite and then finalized after 399 fuzz comparisons.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a longer single-agent run, no timeout, and spent extra budget on iterative edge-case probing and fixes before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained speed from delegation but paid a coordination recovery cost; serial spent more time on black-box refinement without coordination overhead.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both completed official evaluations failed with 58 of 70 testcases. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: parallel used a three-child decomposition and recovered from a bech32core.mjs source overwrite, while serial stayed single-actor and used later probes to remove a length restriction. The available official records do not reveal which hidden cases failed, so the parallel overwrite is retained only as an adverse coordination episode, not as a proven cause of an outcome gap.
parallel_contributors: Three-child delegation produced a same-library overwrite and rework before parent integration.
Parallel retained the standard <=90 bech32 length behavior in the final described output.
serial_contributors: Single main actor avoided cross-agent file ownership conflicts.
Serial found and patched a long-address executable mismatch before final checks.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial removed the max-address-length check after probing; parallel did not.
Both passed extensive local comparisons yet failed the official hidden set, whose failing cases are not exposed in the allowed inputs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome difference; retained coordination issue is adverse but not outcome-differential

candidates.reason: Implementation owners existed: children produced core, segwit, CLI, and formatting modules, and the parent produced the entrypoint.
The parent explicitly inspected child modules and integrated them into test5.mjs after the swarm returned.
The parent owned and wrote the required entrypoint and delivered the final /output tree.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition from probing through delegation, assembly, verification, cleanup, and final response.
The parent did initial probes before delegation, but productive implementation was not blocked behind a failed mandatory preflight or shortened closure window.
Parallel did not run only investigators first; it delegated implementation modules and then integrated them.
No indispensable path was left under-resourced by auxiliary work; parent assembled and verified after all child results.
Only three children were launched, the run did not time out, and there is no evidence that breadth exhausted the finite budget.
No child was given an overbroad scope that remained unfinished; each child returned completed assigned modules or tests.
Child briefs included the relevant module contracts and acceptance examples; the long-address mismatch was not a known parent fact omitted from a child brief.
The parent specified module import/export contracts; the realized failure was a concrete same-source replacement, which is classified under Concurrent Writes.
No known finding or constraint is shown disappearing through a summary or transfer and causing repeated work.
The child handoffs were long but the parent inspected the files and used the results; there is no unconsumed bulk causing unfinished work.
No parent action consumed a superseded handoff after a newer state was visible; the parent reread current files before assembly.
Although one child reported an overwrite, the parent did not receive unresolved incompatible final contracts; it inspected and used the restored files.
The parent made a completion statement after integrated comparisons; no visible unresolved integrated mismatch remained before closure.
There was no replacement child or retry that lacked inherited findings and repeated prior work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No active child was explicitly stopped, cancelled, or interrupted before its needed result was finalized.
The parent promoted and delivered a candidate before closure; no complete packageable candidate was left unplaced due to timing.
Parent verification happened after reading child modules and writing the entrypoint; no child result was merged only after the relevant final check.
Delegated implementations were retrievable and the parent read and integrated the modules before final verification.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; child test results were returned in handoffs.
No required child failed or was cancelled without parent takeover; the observed child source overwrite was handled by restoration and parent inspection.
The parent consumed the AgentSwarm result and inspected the completed module files before assembling the final entrypoint.
The parent did not wait until timeout or near a deadline without inspection; it continued after the swarm result and ran checks.
The observed conflict was on the same source file, not competing designs spread across different files.
Two children edited the same file, but one replaced a non-entry source owned by the other, making Source Overwrite the more specific label.
Agent-0 wrote and owned bech32core.mjs, agent-1 later wrote the same non-entry source as a fallback, and agent-0 observed missing exports and restored its version.
candidates.realized_consequence: Agent-0's import/export test failed against the overwritten source and the child had to inspect and restore bech32core.mjs before the parent could rely on it.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file editing is present, but a wholesale replacement of another child-owned non-entry source is the higher-precedence Source Overwrite category.

candidates.reason: The overwritten file was a library module, not the required executable entrypoint or submitted artifact.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced multiple current outputs in the final workspace.
The shared workspace caused a specific source overwrite, so the residual unisolated-write label is less precise and not separately retained.
No generated fixture, cache, temp path, or auxiliary artifact from one actor was consumed by another as stable reference input.

retained_patterns.reason: The segwit child replaced the same non-entry source file that the core child had already written, and the core child then observed a missing-export failure and restored its implementation.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Agent-0's import/export test failed against the overwritten source and the child had to inspect and restore bech32core.mjs before the parent could rely on it.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Same-file editing is present, but a wholesale replacement of another child-owned non-entry source is the higher-precedence Source Overwrite category.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision suppressed for the same bech32core.mjs write chain because Source Overwrite is more specific.
Unisolated Workspace Writes suppressed because the concrete source replacement explains the shared-state consequence.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; the only retained adverse parallel coordination event is the bech32core.mjs source overwrite.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No downstream lifecycle, context, load, or acceptance label is added for the same overwrite-and-restoration chain.
